wy_blue_marble_wall_the.blurb: The Blue Marble Wall is the first of the four tiers that make up the 4 Stories cliff in the Snowy Range above Laramie, sitting at roughly 8,600 feet on national forest land. It is a compact sport wall of short pitches, none much over 60 feet, with a couple of very easy lines and then a thick middle of 5.10 and 5.11 climbs and a handful of 5.12s. The high elevation means cool days in summer but quick afternoon weather changes. Anchors are open cold shuts, and the cable path above the wall is the usual way to rig a top rope; it is entered from the west end. Expect a fairly new crag, so watch for loose rock and wear a helmet.
